newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Former Zaire PM denies fled with state funds.
newsitem.headline: Former Zaire PM denies fled with state funds.

text.p: Zaire's former prime minister Kengo wa Dondo, who a new minister suggested earlier this week had fled the country with part of the national treasury, denied on Thursday he had absconded with state funds.
He told Reuters at his Geneva hotel that he had left the capital Kinshasa by plane "perfectly normally" last Sunday and come to Switzerland for a routine health check.
"I have not fled. Everyone saw me leave at the airport. I have no national treasury money with me," said Kengo, who was voted out of office three weeks ago as Zaire's political crisis mounted.
On Tuesday, Information Minister Kin-Kiey Malumba said an international warrant was being issued for Kengo after officials had found the national treasury empty when he left office.

But Zaire's ambassador in Belgium said on Wednesday no arrest warrant had yet been issued for the former premier. The envoy, Kimbulu Moyanso wa Lokwa, also said Kengo had left Kinshasa openly through the international Ndjili airport.

Kengo said on Thursday he visited Switzerland every year for a health check and would be leaving early next week for another European country. He said he had a visa that allowed him to visit member states of the European Union.
He would then return to Zaire, he said. "I will be ready to answer any allegations against me," he added.
On Wednesday, Swiss officials confirmed he had entered the country with a valid visa and said they had not been informed of any arrest warrant against him.
Kengo has been widely accused in Kinshasa of weakness in dealing with the Tutsi-dominated rebels fighting to topple Zaire's long-time leader Mobutu Sese Seko.

Switzerland was embarrassed over Mobutu's long stay in Lausanne late last year during which he underwent cancer treatment. The Alpine nation, in a calculated snub after Mobutu left in November, announced it had denied him a re-entry visa.
